subject.title: fix(setup): validate current OpenClaw package lifecycle

question: Should the Windows Companion change its default Gateway package to `2026.7.1` before the official LKG setup-connect E2E path passes on the current PR head?
rationale: The branch deliberately makes a release-selection change, and candidate-composition success cannot determine whether maintainers accept a failing supported onboarding path as the new default.

options.title: Gate the LKG bump on official proof
options.body: Keep or restore the existing default until a current-head run shows the unmodified official `2026.7.1` package completing setup-connect successfully.

options.title: Split integrity hardening
options.body: Land only the bounded composed-package digest contract if it can be separated cleanly, then carry the LKG/version-policy change in a later proof-positive PR.

options.title: Accept the release risk
options.body: Intentionally ship `2026.7.1` as the default despite the failed official E2E lane, with an explicit support and rollback plan.

recommendation.title: Gate the LKG bump on official proof
recommendation.body: Keep or restore the existing default until a current-head run shows the unmodified official `2026.7.1` package completing setup-connect successfully.

likelyOwner.reason: CassieMei authored the branch commits that establish the LKG, package-selection, and setup lifecycle contract, though ownership confidence is limited without inspectable current-main history.
